sentences.text: Akkermansia muciniphila is a mucin-degrading bacterium residing in the human gut, and a review reports it constitutes roughly three to five percent of the gut microbiota in healthy adults.

Longitudinal metagenomic data from seven healthy individuals showed fluctuating relative abundance with short-term blooms, and detection rates of 56.9 percent by 16S sequencing and 33.3 percent by whole-genome sequencing.

That study reported closely related strains shared between cohabiting individuals and across China, South Korea and the United States, which the authors read as human-mediated or environmental transmission.
A narrative review describes its abundance as linked to health with a reduction commonly observed in obesity, while noting concerns about potential pro-inflammatory effects at high concentrations.
Another review reports that depletion of Akkermansia muciniphila is associated with age-related diseases whereas its abundance is enriched in healthy centenarians.
